Subject: ACME: Post-call recap — concurrency & latency targets (next steps)

Thanks for the call today — quick recap and next steps so we have a single place to track items. Nice to meet you, Sofia. Looping in Laura (solutions engineer) and Michael (CS) to scope the pilot.

Key requirements we captured today:
- Latency/SLOs: p95 token latency target for short completions ~< 150 ms; end-to-end request p95 (including network) target < 250 ms for single-turn API calls. For streaming, we need stable token delivery with per-token latency ~< 120 ms and max time to first token < 200 ms.
- Throughput & concurrency: sustained baseline of ~250 concurrent requests (parallel user requests), with expected spikes up to ~400 for short windows (1-2 minutes).
- Payloads & models: most calls are short completions (avg 30-80 tokens) with occasional long-running streams (60-90s) for multi-turn sessions. Context windows: up to 8k tokens for a subset (rare).
- Connection pooling: client will use HTTP/2 where possible; prefer guidance on connection count, keep-alive, and connection-per-core recommendations.

As discussed, the items we need from Redwood to proceed to a pilot / quote: 
1) Confirmation on default Redwood rate limits (concurrency & QPS) and how we can scale them for ACME (reserved capacity vs. burst).
2) Recommended client conn pool config for HTTP/2 and guidance on behavior when hitting limits (429 vs queued).
3) A proposed pilot plan and cost estimate for reserved capacity that guarantees 250 concurrency (with burst to 400).

Attachments: ACME-SLO-draft-20260720.pdf (SLO summary), Redwood-rate-limits-sheet-20260720.xlsx (Redwood default limits + add-on tiers).

Proposed next steps:
- Laura: technical deep-dive / load test plan (we discussed early next week)
- Michael: pilot quote and procurement-friendly terms (include monthly committed concurrency level + burst options)
- Sofia / Procurement: confirm timeline for procurement review and any CIT or security questionnaire items we should expect

Thanks — I can set up the technical deep-dive for Tue/Wed next week if that works.

Best,

Subject: Re: ACME: Post-call recap — concurrency & latency targets (technical notes)

Sofia — quick technical notes from our side (happy to go deeper on the call):

Redwood defaults (hosted API):
- Per-org default concurrency: 100 concurrent requests
- Per-API-key default QPS: 200 requests/sec (short-lived bursts allowed)
- Streaming connections counted against concurrency while open

Options to meet ACME targets:
- Reserved capacity (Dedicated): we can guarantee N concurrent requests (isolated pool). For the pilot we'd recommend reserving 250 concurrency with configured burst buffer to 400 for short windows. This is a monthly committed SKU (can be scaled quarterly).
- Autoscaling + burst: hosted customers can use autoscaling, but guaranteed concurrency is only via reserved capacity. We offer configurable burst credits for occasional spikes — typically sized as % over commit for a billing window.

Client recommendations (connection pooling):
- Use HTTP/2 where possible (multiplexing reduces connections and improves throughput). Redwood supports long-lived streams over HTTP/2 and HTTP/1.1 chunked.
- Keep-Alive: enable TCP keep-alive and aggressive reuse; we recommend ~60s keep-alive for client pools.
- Connection counts: for large-scale clients, target ~25-100 connections per client host and rely on multiplexing; if using HTTP/1.1, distribute across more connections (50+).
- Backpressure: on 429s, use exponential backoff + jitter and respect Retry-After. For streaming, if the connection is accepted but tokens are delayed, we provide prefix caching and KV cache hints to reduce repeated work.

Notes on long streams and resource accounting: each open streaming session consumes a slot from the reserved concurrency pool. For 90s streams, that means those sessions will reduce headroom for short completions during spikes unless reserved capacity accounts for them. One common pattern: route streaming sessions to a separate reserved pool or lower-cost backend with longer-lived instances to avoid impacting short-turn latency.

I'll prepare a short load-test plan and recommended client settings before the deep-dive.

—Laura

Proposed pilot (3 weeks):

- Burst capacity: up to 400 concurrent requests for 5-minute windows (burst credits applied)
- Models: mixed workload (13B for baseline; larger model routed to separate pool to avoid headroom contention)
- Observability: 30-day token + request-level tracing, per-route latency dashboards, and SLIs for p50/p95/p99 token latency
- Estimated cost (pilot): monthly-equivalent commitment prorated for 3 weeks — see attached pilot-quote stub. Final pricing will reflect model CPU/GPU mix; we'll provide a line-item quote after you confirm model split.

Action items:
1) ACME: confirm model split (approx % volume per model) and expected average tokens (Sofia noted ~45).

3) Laura: deliver load-test plan and client config by Tue EOD.
4) Procurement: confirm timeline for signing and any PO/process requirements.

I've attached a pilot-quote stub (Redwood-rate-limits-sheet-20260720.xlsx) and will follow up with a formal DocuSign once we finalize the commit level.
